cues.zh: 帮助人们学习最有效的方式是：惩罚还是奖励？

cues.zh: 想想以色列战斗机飞行员的训练案例，因为那里的教官
cues.en: Well, consider the case of Israeli fighter pilot training, because instructors there

cues.zh: 发现负面反馈远比正面反馈有效。
cues.en: found that negative feedback was far superior to positive feedback.

cues.zh: 如果学员的某个动作做得特别差，教官就会训斥他。
cues.en: If a cadet performed a particularly poor maneuver they would reprimand him.

cues.zh: 但他们注意到，在后续尝试中，他的表现总是会提高。
cues.en: But they noticed that on follow up attempts, his performance invariably improved.

cues.zh: 相反，如果他们表扬学员完成了某个熟练的飞行动作，他在后续
cues.en: In contrast, if they praised a cadet for executing a skillful maneuver, his performance on subsequent

cues.zh: 尝试中的表现通常会下降。
cues.en: attempts typically declined.

cues.zh: 所以他们自然得出结论：正面反馈无效，甚至有害，
cues.en: So naturally they concluded that positive feedback is ineffective or even detrimental

cues.zh: 而负面反馈才管用。
cues.en: whereas negative feedback is what works.

cues.zh: 问题在于，这似乎与大量研究表明正面反馈
cues.en: The problem is this seems to contradict a body of research that shows positive feedback

cues.zh: 实际上比负面反馈更有效相矛盾。
cues.en: is actually more effective than negative feedback.

cues.zh: 例如，在涉及教师的研究中发现，如果老师提高
cues.en: For example, in studies involving teachers it was found that if a teacher increase the

cues.zh: 正面反馈与负面反馈的比例，这实际上会增加
cues.en: ratio of positive feedback to negative feedback, that actually increases the percentage of

cues.zh: 学生投入任务的时间百分比。
cues.en: times students spend on task.

cues.zh: 在另一项研究中，橄榄球运动员在一场比赛后接受了视频反馈环节，
cues.en: In another study rugby players were given a video feedback session following a game,

cues.zh: 只不过其中一半人被展示了他们的精彩片段，并因他们的表现受到表扬，
cues.en: except half of them were shown their highlights and they were praised for what they had done

cues.zh: 而另一半人则被展示了他们最大的失误、他们的错误。
cues.en: and the other half were shown their biggest blunders, their mistakes.

cues.zh: 他们因做错事而受到训斥。
cues.en: And they were scolded for doing things incorrectly.

cues.zh: 一周后在下一场比赛中，正是那些接受了正面
cues.en: Now a week later at the next game, it was the players who had received the positive

cues.zh: 强化的球员表现最好。
cues.en: reinforcement who performed the best.

cues.zh: 而且事实上，这种差异不仅仅是心理层面的。
cues.en: And, in fact, the difference was not just psychological.

cues.zh: 血液检测显示，接受正面反馈的球员实际上比
cues.en: Blood tests revealed that the players who received positive feedback actually had higher

cues.zh: 接受负面反馈的球员拥有更高水平的睾酮。
cues.en: levels of testosterone than players who had received the negative feedback.

cues.zh: 我认为相当值得注意的一点是，即使反馈过去一周了，你仍然能看到
cues.en: I think that is quite remarkable that even a week post feedback you could still see a

cues.zh: 两种反馈类型之间存在生理上的差异。
cues.en: physiological difference between the two types of feedback.

cues.zh: 哇。
cues.en: Wow.

cues.zh: 那么为什么这对以色列战斗机飞行员不起作用呢？
cues.en: Well so why didn't this work for the Israeli fighter pilots?

cues.zh: 嗯，也许存在文化差异，在某些文化中负面反馈效果
cues.en: Well, maybe there are cultural differences and in some cultures negative feedback works

cues.zh: 更好。
cues.en: better.

cues.zh: 或者也许这取决于任务。
cues.en: Or maybe it is task dependent.

cues.zh: 也许某些技能，比如学习驾驶战斗机，需要更多的负面反馈。
cues.en: Perhaps some skills like learning to fly a fighter jet require more negative feedback.

cues.zh: 又或者反馈与战斗机飞行员的表现根本毫无关系。
cues.en: Or maybe the feedback had nothing to do with the performance of the fighter pilots at all.

cues.zh: 也许无论收到什么反馈，他们的表现都会一样。
cues.en: Maybe they would have performed in the same way regardless of the feedback they received.

cues.zh: 听我接着说。
cues.en: Go with me on this.

cues.zh: 想象有100名学生参加一场考试，考试包含100道对错题
cues.en: Imagine you have 100 students taking a test which consists of 100 true or false questions

cues.zh: 内容是他们一无所知的科目。
cues.en: on a subject they know nothing about.

cues.zh: 现在假设他们都随机作答，我们知道最终的分数分布
cues.en: Now assuming they all answer randomly, we know that the resulting distribution of scores

cues.zh: 平均分会在50左右。
cues.en: will have an average of around 50.

cues.zh: 但纯凭运气，有些学生的得分会明显高于或低于
cues.en: But just by chance, some students will have scored significantly better or worse than

cues.zh: 平均分。
cues.en: the average.

cues.zh: >> 哦，天哪。
cues.en: >> Oh, man.

cues.zh: >> 如果你选出得分都高于50的前10名学生，再给他们做一次
cues.en: >> If you select the top 10 students whose scores were all above 50 and gave them a second

cues.zh: 非常类似的测试，你会发现他们的平均分会回落到
cues.en: very similar test, you would find that the average of their scores would drop back to

cues.zh: 50左右。
cues.en: around 50.

cues.zh: 同样，如果你选出垫底的10名学生，他们后续测试的分数会回升
cues.en: Similarly, if you selected the bottom 10 students, their score on a subsequent test would rise
to 50.

cues.zh: 这就是均值回归。
cues.en: This is just regression to the mean.

cues.zh: 均值回归就是为什么如果你今天高尔夫打得特别好，
cues.en: Regression to the mean is the reason why if you have a really good round of golf today,

cues.zh: 明天的成绩就不会那么好。
cues.en: your round tomorrow will not be as good.

cues.zh: 是的。
cues.en: Yes.

cues.zh: 这是因为随机运气几乎在我们做的每件事中都起作用。
cues.en: That is because random chance plays a role in virtually everything that we do.

cues.zh: 事件的结果既受我们的能力影响，也受一点运气影响。
cues.en: So the outcomes of events are influenced by both our skill and a little bit of luck.

cues.zh: 所以如果你某一天运气特别好，那么第二天的运气水平很可能
cues.en: So if you have especially good luck on one day, chances are your level of luck will not

cues.zh: 就没那么好了。
cues.en: be as good the next day.

cues.zh: 这听起来有点像赌徒谬误，它认为过去的事件会影响
cues.en: Now that sounds a little bit like the gamblers fallacy, which states that past events influence

cues.zh: 未来的概率。
cues.en: future probabilities.

cues.zh: 比如，你抛硬币，连续几次都是反面，赌徒谬误
cues.en: For example, if you flip a coin and it comes up tails a couple of times, the gamblers fallacy

cues.zh: 就是期待下一次抛硬币正面的概率会增加。
cues.en: is to expect the probability of heads to increase for the next flip.

cues.zh: 实际上并不会。
cues.en: In reality it doesn’t.

cues.zh: 仍然是50比50。
cues.en: It is still 50-50.

cues.zh: 赌徒谬误的想法是，概率会变化，以便总体上事情
cues.en: The idea wit the gamblers fallacy is that probabilities change so that overall things

cues.zh: 在长期内趋于平衡。
cues.en: over out in the long run.

cues.zh: 就是这个想法。
cues.en: That is the idea.

cues.zh: 而在均值回归中，并不是事情在趋于平衡，只是极端
cues.en: With regression to the mean, it is not that things are evening out, it is just that extreme

cues.zh: 事件被更常发生的平均事件稀释了。
cues.en: events are becoming diluted by the average events which happen much more commonly.

cues.zh: 现在这些学生每道题都完全靠猜。
cues.en: Now with these students they were completely guessing on every question.

cues.zh: 但即使你对这个主题有所了解，仍然会有
cues.en: But even when you know something about the subject, there is still going to be there

cues.zh: 那种运气成分。
cues.en: that element of chance.

cues.zh: 所以均值回归总会发生，只是程度较小。
cues.en: And so regression to the mean always occurs, just to a lesser extent.

cues.zh: 这在研究中非常值得考虑。
cues.en: This is really important to consider in research.

cues.zh: 想象你在试验一种预防心脏病的新药。
cues.en: Imagine you are trialing a new drug to help prevent heart disease.

cues.zh: 你从患者样本中挑选出心脏健康指标最低的10%的人，
cues.en: So from a sample of patients you select those in the bottom 10 percent of heart health indicators,

cues.en: people with high blood pressure, high cholesterol, that sort of thing.

cues.zh: 用药一个月后，你再次检测他们，发现他们的分数
cues.en: Now after a month of being on a drug, you test them again to find that their scores

cues.zh: 有所改善。
cues.en: have improved.

cues.zh: 很好，药物起作用了，对吧？
cues.en: Well, great, the drug is working, right?

cues.zh: 嗯，也许并非如此。
cues.en: Well, maybe not.

cues.zh: 问题在于，虽然血压和胆固醇比，比如说，
cues.en: See, the trouble is that although blood pressure and cholesterol are more stable than, say,

cues.zh: 随机判断题的分数更稳定，但仍然存在一些固有的变异性，
cues.en: your score on a random true or false test, there is still some inherent variability caused

cues.zh: 比如当天的压力水平、最近的饮食，甚至
cues.en: by, say, your level of stress on the day or your recent diet or even the uncertainties

cues.zh: 测量仪器引入的不确定性。
cues.en: introduced by the measuring apparatus.

cues.zh: 所以在第一次测试中排在最后10%的人，很可能这些
cues.en: So the people who ended up in the bottom 10 percent on the first test, likely had these

cues.zh: 因素都对他们不利。
cues.en: factors all count against them.

cues.zh: 他们特别不走运。
cues.en: They were particularly unlucky.

cues.zh: 但你不该指望第二次测试时他们还那么不走运。
cues.en: But you should not expect them to be as unlucky when you test them a second time.

cues.zh: 所以他们的分数应该仅凭随机机会就会提高。
cues.en: So their scores should improve just based on random chance.

cues.zh: 这就是为什么临床试验必须使用对照组，而且对照组要从完全
cues.en: That is why it is so important that clinical trials use control groups drawn from exactly

cues.zh: 相同的人群中抽取，这样你才能看出药物是否比单纯的随机
cues.en: the same population so that you can see whether the drug improves scores more than random

cues.zh: 机会更能提高分数。
cues.en: chance alone would.
